start_here: Say to your AI: "Run workflow:keep-my-changes-to-the-shipped-defaults with store {\"where\": \"postgresql database example_me on my own computer\", \"language\": \"SQL (PostgreSQL)\", \"credential_name\": \"example-me-postgres-connection\"}, shipped_ids [\"rule:a\", \"rule:b\", \"schedule:c\"] and changes [{\"default_id\": \"rule:b\", \"change\": \"remove\"}]."
no_lists_because: It names no list: the person's changes to the shipped defaults are kept in the person's own store, in whatever form that store keeps things, and the shipped defaults come from the deploy, handed in with each run.
instructions: 1. Keep the store's login in your vault under a name you choose, and say where the store is and how it is spoken to.
2. Say "Run workflow:keep-my-changes-to-the-shipped-defaults" with store, the shipped_ids the deploy ships now, and the changes to keep.
3. The first run makes the store's own objects once and proves them on the example attempts; every attempt must be kept, repeated or refused as the intent says, or the run stops and says which.
4. Every later run keeps the new changes and reads each shipped default's state back: on, off, edited (with the person's words) or removed.

worked_examples.title: A default removed, kept once
worked_examples.ask: Remove the example rule rule:b from my defaults.

store.where: postgresql database example_me on my own computer

worked_examples.given: The look step found no changes kept, made by an earlier run; the three shipped defaults are on.
worked_examples.hands_back: kept ["rule:b"]; found shows rule:a on, rule:b removed and schedule:c on. A later deploy that edits rule:a still reaches this account, because the person never changed rule:a.
